name: American Community Survey 5-year estimates (detailed tables)
agency: U.S. Census Bureau
description: Survey-based period estimates with 90% margins of error for all geographies down to block groups, released annually.
access_requirements: Free Census API key required for every request (verified 2026-09-28: keyless requests are redirected to missing_key.html)
history_notes: Multiyear tabulations use final-year boundaries; dollars adjusted to the final year with national CPI-U; 2020 data collection disruption increased MOEs in releases containing 2020; tables added/changed over time (e.g. B23025, B15003 from 2010-2014/2008-2012; B28002 from 2013-2017).
suppression_rules: Estimates with too few sample cases are published as special values (-666666666 etc.) and treated as insufficient_sample.
limitations: Period estimates; not for single-year change. Small-area MOEs can be large.
doc_evidence: ACS Accuracy of the Data (2020-2024) and API dataset list fetched; 5-year datasets listed for 2009-2024 in api.census.gov/data.json

name: National Database of Childcare Prices (NDCP) county-level file 2008-2022
agency: U.S. Department of Labor Women's Bureau
description: County-level median and 75th-percentile full-time weekly childcare prices by provider type (center-based vs family child care home) and child age (11 six-month bands plus infant, toddler, preschool and school-age aggregates), compiled by ICF from state market rate surveys with imputations; bundled with ACS labor, income and demographic covariates.
access_requirements: None for the xlsx (91.7 MB, one sheet). DOL API https://apiprod.dol.gov/v4/get/WB/ndcp/json (dataset id 10278) requires a free DOL API key (HTTP 401 without key).
license: U.S. federal government work (public domain per DOL copyright notice), no dataset-specific license stated
time_coverage: 2008-2022 annual study years (48,308 county-year rows, 3,220-3,221 counties per year, 50 states + DC + PR)
update_cadence: Irregular: original 2008-2018 database created 2019, Nov 2024 update added 2019-2022 (DOL API frequency Ad-Hoc)
history_notes: 2024 update added 2019-2022 and Puerto Rico and added between-study-year imputations to 2008-2018 (Appendix I). 2008 ACS covariates from 3-year ACS (counties 20k+). Superseded 2008-2018 file: /sites/dolgov/files/WB/media/nationaldatabaseofchildcareprices.xlsx (35 MB).
suppression_rules: Survey reports with fewer than 10 providers masked or counties clustered. Price imputations flagged by 5-digit text flags i* (digits: other age group, weekly conversion, statewide-to-county model, 50th/75th percentile, between-study-year); *_flag 1/2/3 shows how aggregate age groups were derived.
limitations: No price data for Indiana or New Mexico in any year; Missouri only 2015-2020; Colorado only 2014, 2015, 2022. Prices come from market rate surveys of regulated providers, often rate-zone values repeated across counties, and are heavily imputed; not family out-of-pocket spending. COUNTY_FIPS_CODE is numeric (pad to 5 digits).
doc_evidence: Read Sept 2024 technical report PDF (2.28 MB): Appendix C defines MC*/MFCC* as median full-time weekly prices and _75* as 75th percentile; imputation methods pp.6-21.
sample_evidence: Downloaded NDCP2022.xlsx (91,691,849 bytes): 48,308 rows x 370 cols. Travis Co TX (48453) 2022 MCINFANT = 229 dollars/week. Saved 90-row extract ndcp_sample.csv.

description: State x year x care type (Center, Family) median weekly prices for infant, toddler, preschool and school-age care; percent of children living in counties in each national price quintile and affordability quintile (price as % of median family income); estimated child populations; percent of children in counties with valid prices.
access_requirements: None (417 KB xlsx; single sheet named 'State Child Care Affordability ' with a trailing space)
license: U.S. federal government work (public domain per DOL copyright notice), no dataset-specific license stated
time_coverage: 2008-2022 annual (1,560 rows = 52 states/DC/PR x 15 years x 2 care types)
update_cadence: Irregular (issued Nov 2024 with the county update)

suppression_rules: Rows exist but values are blank where no county prices exist (e.g., Indiana, New Mexico). PCT_VALID_* gives the share of children in counties with price estimates.
limitations: DOL cautions that state medians mask large within-state variation and limit state rankings. Affordability uses median family income. data.gov lists a technical report URL (NDCP2022-Technical-Report-508.pdf) that returns HTTP 404.
doc_evidence: Appendix E of the Sept 2024 technical report defines PRICE_Q*, AFFORDABILITY_Q* (price as % of median family income) and MEDIAN_*_PRICE for the state file.

name: County Business Patterns (CBP): establishments, employment and payroll by NAICS industry

name: LEHD Origin-Destination Employment Statistics (LODES) version 8.4
agency: U.S. Census Bureau, Center for Economic Studies (LEHD program) with state partners
description: Job counts at 2020 census block level for workplaces (WAC), residences (RAC) and home-to-work pairs (OD) by job type, worker age, monthly earnings band and NAICS sector; race/ethnicity/education/sex from 2009; firm age/size from 2011 (JT02 only).
access_requirements: None. File patterns: {st}/wac/{st}_wac_{SEG}_{JT}_{YEAR}.csv.gz; {st}/rac/{st}_rac_{SEG}_{JT}_{YEAR}.csv.gz; {st}/od/{st}_od_{main|aux}_{JT}_{YEAR}.csv.gz; {st}_xwalk.csv.gz block crosswalk
license: Public-use Census Bureau data (U.S. federal government work); LEHD data page gives a requested citation format
geo_levels: state;county;cousub;place;tract;bg;zcta;cbsa;cd;sd;other:2020 census block (crosswalk also carries state legislative districts, tribal areas, workforce investment areas)
time_coverage: 2002-2023 for most states (data vintage 20251202). No OD/WAC files: AK 2017-2023, MI 2022-2023, MA 2002-2010, DC 2002-2009, AR and NH 2002, AZ and MS 2002-2003. Puerto Rico not included.
history_notes: LODES8 uses 2020 blocks (LODES7 used 2010 blocks); federal (OPM) job types from 2010; worker demographics from 2009; job frame limited to ages 14-99 from 2012; earnings bands are fixed nominal thresholds ($1,250 and $3,333 per month).
suppression_rules: No cell suppression; Census disclosure avoidance review (CBDRB-FY21-249); state-years lacking employment data have RAC files only.
limitations: Counts jobs, not people (JT01 primary jobs approximates workers); administrative job frame (state UI records plus federal OPM), so self-employment is not covered; residence side partly modeled.
doc_evidence: Tech doc 8.4 (Rev. 20251203): OD/RAC/WAC at census block, years 2002-2023, state-year gap table (AK 2017+, MI 2022-23), file-name templates and variable lists.
sample_evidence: de_wac_S000_JT00_2023.csv.gz (175 KB): 7,383 blocks, 450,843 jobs (New Castle Co 298,174). Directory listings: AK WAC ends 2016, MI WAC ends 2021, MI RAC runs to 2023.

name: Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS)
agency: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, National Center for Statistics and Analysis
description: Census of fatal motor-vehicle crashes on trafficways open to the public (death within 30 days) with accident, vehicle, person and related files; crash location coded with GSA county and city codes and latitude/longitude (1999+).
access_requirements: None for static zip files; nhtsa.gov web pages and the CrashAPI returned HTTP 403 to scripted requests from this environment
license: U.S. federal government work (no copyright); no license terms found in files
time_coverage: 1975-2023 final files; 2024 Annual Report File (first release 2026-04-01)
update_cadence: Annual; the Annual Report File is replaced by a Final file about a year later
history_notes: COUNTY and CITY use GSA Geographic Location Codes (manual: codes occasionally divided); coordinates from 1999; data elements added and discontinued over time (documented in the Analytical User's Manual).
suppression_rules: None (census of qualifying crashes; no personal identifiers).
limitations: Location is where the crash occurred, not victims' residence; small annual counts in small counties (use multi-year sums); excludes non-fatal and non-trafficway crashes; manual covers Puerto Rico but the 2023 national CSV held 51 state codes.
doc_evidence: Manual DOT HS 813 794 (Apr 2026): census of fatal crashes, death within 30 days; COUNTY uses GSA codes; ARF later replaced by final file. Release notes: 2023 final file 2026-04-01.
sample_evidence: FARS2023NationalCSV.zip (34.2 MB): accident.csv 37,769 fatal crashes and 41,025 deaths across 51 state codes; person.csv 7,367 pedestrian and 1,163 bicyclist deaths.

name: FCC Broadband Data Collection (BDC) / National Broadband Map
agency: Federal Communications Commission
description: Provider-reported fixed broadband availability by Broadband Serviceable Location (technology, maximum advertised speeds, business/residential) and mobile coverage; Fixed Broadband Summary by Geography gives the share of BSL units served at 0.2/0.2, 10/1, 25/3, 100/20, 250/25 and 1000/100 Mbps by technology group.
access_requirements: Website downloads showed no login step (disclaimer only). Public Data API (bdc.fcc.gov/api/public/map/...) needs an FCC User Registration account and a generated token sent as username and hash_value headers; 10 calls per minute. fcc.gov hosts returned 403 to curl.
license: FCC public data; no explicit open license found; API token generation requires accepting FCC terms; Fabric location attributes (address, coordinates) are licensed via CostQuest and not public
geo_levels: nation;state;county;cd;place;cbsa;other:tribal areas;other:census block and H3 hexagon via location-level files
time_coverage: As-of dates 2022-06-30 through 2025-12-31, semiannual (8 vintages; data download page last updated 2026-09-15)
update_cadence: Semiannual (June 30 and December 31 as-of dates); earlier vintages revised after challenges (file names carry revision dates)
history_notes: Location-based BDC method (from June 2022) replaced Form 477 census-block reporting (last as of June 2021); the two series are not comparable. Location Fabric changes each filing round; summary-by-geography files restructured (spec v2.4.3, Aug 2026).
suppression_rules: None; public files identify locations only by Location ID.
limitations: Maximum advertised speeds reported by providers, not measured performance, price or adoption; satellite inflates any-technology coverage; values change as challenges are resolved.
doc_evidence: Download spec (Aug 11, 2026) defines summary files with share of units served per speed tier; API spec (Jun 8, 2026) requires account plus token; NBM page lists Jun 30, 2022-Dec 31, 2025.
sample_evidence: curl and WebFetch to broadbandmap.fcc.gov and fcc.gov returned 403; API needs registration; download page viewed in a browser (links present, nothing downloaded).

name: FCC Form 477 Fixed Broadband Deployment Data and Area Tables (legacy, to June 2021)
agency: Federal Communications Commission
description: Provider filings listing census blocks where fixed service is or could be offered (technology, maximum advertised speeds); Area Tables summarize population by number of fixed providers at speed tiers by geography with urban/rural and tribal splits.
access_requirements: None (Socrata SODA API; app token optional)

history_notes: Multiple versions per period (V1/V2); speed tiers 0.2 to 1000 Mbps; area tables use 2010 Census urban/rural and tribal flags; not comparable with BDC location-level data.
suppression_rules: None
limitations: A census block counts as served if a provider can serve at least one location in it, which overstates coverage; advertised speeds only; population-based coverage.

name: FBI Crime Data Explorer (UCR: SRS and NIBRS offenses, arrests, law enforcement employees)
agency: Federal Bureau of Investigation, CJIS Division, Uniform Crime Reporting Program
description: Agency-level offenses known to police (Summary Reporting System and incident-based NIBRS), clearances, arrests, law enforcement employees and participation; national/state estimates; bulk CSV and master-file downloads and a Crime Data API (JSON/CSV).
access_requirements: Free api.data.gov key (API returned 403 API_KEY_MISSING without a key); bulk files at https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/webapp/#/pages/downloads need no key
license: U.S. federal government work (public domain); FBI advises against ranking or comparing states or other entities except a city to its state and a state to the nation
time_coverage: Agency monthly series from 1985 (API); annual data through 2025 (released August 2026); NIBRS files by state and year
update_cadence: Annual release (August-September) plus monthly year-to-date master files
history_notes: SRS retired January 2021: 2021 data NIBRS-only with large gaps (CDE US population coverage averaged about 77% in 2021 vs about 96% in 2020 and 95% in 2022); NIBRS records all offenses in an incident while SRS used a hierarchy rule; estimation methods developed with BJS.
suppression_rules: No suppression of agency counts; UCR participation data identify partial reporters; national/state totals are estimated for non-reporting agencies.
limitations: Voluntary reporting of offenses known to police; agency jurisdictions do not match Census places; overlapping agencies (sheriffs, state police) complicate county totals.
doc_evidence: CDE API docs (browser): base api.usa.gov/crime/fbi/cde, link to get an API key, FBI advises against rankings; Downloads page: 2025 data provided August 2026.
sample_evidence: api.data.gov DEMO_KEY: Dover PD (DE0010100) 2023 violent offenses 381, property 2,192; 105 sworn officers; NY 2021 population coverage 68.9%; monthly data back to 1985.

agency: FEMA U.S. Fire Administration

name: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database
agency: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (from NWS Storm Data)

States are model-based and benchmarked to national CPS; substate areas use Handbook and ACS-share disaggregation.

time_coverage: Monthly Jan 1976- for states, DC, Puerto Rico, Census regions/divisions, New York city and Los Angeles-Long Beach-Glendale MD; Jan 1990- for counties, metros and most cities (cities added when they pass 25,000); latest Aug 2026 (states) and Jul 2026 (substate); annual averages (period M13) for not seasonally adjusted series through 2025

name: IPUMS National Historical Geographic Information System: Version 21.0 [dataset]
agency: Jonathan Schroeder, David Van Riper, Steven Manson, Grace Cooper, Zachary Krause, Tracy Kugler, Tsu Zhu and Steven Ruggles; Minneapolis, MN: IPUMS, University of Minnesota, 2026; http://doi.org/10.18128/D050.V21.0
description: Summary tables from every decennial census 1790-2020, the ACS, County Business Patterns 1970-2002, agricultural censuses and vital statistics (1915-2007); time series tables linking censuses (nominally integrated, and 1990-2020 counts standardized to 2010 units); boundary files 1790-2024; block-based geographic crosswalks.
access_requirements: Free IPUMS account registered for NHGIS (https://uma.pop.umn.edu/nhgis/registration/new) and an API key (IPUMS_API_KEY in .env, sent as the Authorization header); without the NHGIS registration, extract requests return HTTP 401. The metadata API also needs the key; crosswalk downloads redirect to the IPUMS login. R package ipumsr 0.10.0 exists but is not needed (httr2 client in R/providers/nhgis.R).
license: IPUMS NHGIS terms: cite Version 21.0 (doi:10.18128/D050.V21.0); "You will not redistribute the data without permission" (statistics derived for reports are fine; extracts stay in the git-ignored cache; the test fixture is made up)
time_coverage: Decennial 1790-2020: states and counties from 1790, tracts from 1910 (8 cities; whole U.S. from 1990), places and county subdivisions from 1970, block groups from 1990; ACS 5-year 2005-2009 to 2020-2024; CBP 1970-2002 (states and counties)
history_notes: Nominally integrated series link areas by name and code, so they stop when codes change (Connecticut in 2022); standardized series put 1990-2020 counts on 2010 units only (no medians or long-form data yet); race comparisons break in 2000 (multiple races); census income is for the prior calendar year in nominal dollars; the poverty definition changed in 1980; education was measured in years of school through 1980 and degrees from 1990; 1970 sample tables omit places under 2,500.
suppression_rules: As published by the Census Bureau (negative values in 1970 tables mark suppressed cells).
limitations: Used for census years 1970-2000 of seven time series tables (AX6, B69, B79, B84, BD5, C53, CL6) for the nation, regions, divisions, states, counties, county subdivisions and places, as nominally integrated series. One extract (about 6 minutes to produce) is cached. Tracts, boundary files and crosswalks are not used; Connecticut planning regions have no census values. CBP uses SIC industry codes before 1998.

sample_evidence: Extract of AX6, B69, B79, B84, BD5, C53 and CL6, census years, 7 levels: 225,236 area-years. U.S. median household income $16,841 (1979), $30,056 (1989), $41,994 (1999); per capita income $7,298 (1979); 1989 poverty 31,742,864 of 241,977,859 people (13.1%).
